lines.text: Most of us treat forgetting as a failure. I think that's backwards.
Forgetting is part of how memory works.
Your brain lets most things fade, and that's not a bug.
In eighteen eighty-five, the German psychologist Hermann Ebbinghaus published an odd experiment on himself.
He memorized lists of nonsense syllables, like dax, bok and zif, then measured how long they took to relearn.
Memory dropped fastest in the first hours, then leveled off. That's the forgetting curve.
Here's the part people miss. Each time he relearned a list, it faded more slowly.
And spreading practice over several days took far fewer repetitions than cramming it into one.
Cramming feels productive. Spacing actually works.
The best review isn't rereading your notes. It's trying to recall them before you look.
That struggle is the point. Psychologists call it a desirable difficulty.
So when something starts slipping away, don't panic. That's the moment to practice.
For more conversations like this, follow Open Question.
